body:
_sync_legacy_dvc_creds copies user-config credentials into countries_root()/.dvc/s3_creds at import and from _auto_unlock_s3. The reader already passes config.s3_creds_path() to DVCFS, so user-config credentials should not require a package-tree write.

Coordinate __init__.py/data_access.py, the tests/conftest.py credential resolver, test_s3_unlock monkeypatches and scripts/dvc_remote_reachability.py. Preserve an explicit legacy fallback only if policy requires it. Acceptance: import from a read-only installed package performs no credential write there; user-config-only credentials execute requires_s3 tests and still permit source reads. CI's manually created in-tree credentials must not conceal this case. Attach no credentials.

Separate from #810's cwd-rooted data reads and #831's source-file policy. Evidence: slurm_logs/release_landing_2026-10-14/runtime-residuals.org; source symbols remain in the frozen tree.

[Release investigation and reviewed issue disposition](https://github.com/ligon/LSMS_Library/blob/8d7a5e55914e700c69ae1a195f96cc2282b6ce64/slurm_logs/release_landing_2026-10-14/RELEASE_ISSUES.org). This follow-up is separate from the reviewed implementation landings.

comments.body: PR #1022 (`fix/1001-creds`, `66a0a12ee`) resolves this issue (`Closes #1001`, fires on release). Two follow-ups outside its scope are split out: #1031 (CI still writes reader credentials into the tree at `ci.yml:248`/`:390`) and #1032 (DVC itself writes `countries_root()/.dvc/tmp/btime`).

title: Remove runtime credential writes into the installed countries tree
